Cambridge.metaDescription: Rats, raccoons, squirrels and bats in Cambridge, MA — dense multifamily housing from Harvard Square to East Cambridge. Our MassWildlife-licensed PAC crew offers same-day service; call us today.
Cambridge.housing_era: Cambridge is dominated by triple-deckers, two- and three-family wood-frame houses, and older brick apartment buildings, with grand single-family homes in West Cambridge and newer large residential buildings around Kendall Square and Lechmere.
Cambridge.geographic_features: Charles River (southern border, with riverside parks and rowing houses), Fresh Pond (reservoir and wooded reservation in West Cambridge), Alewife Brook (western edge near the Alewife reservation), Danehy Park (built green space in North Cambridge)
neighborhoods: Harvard Square (historic core around Harvard University)

Cambridge.wildlife_intro:
Cambridge pairs very dense older housing with the Charles River and Fresh Pond, and most of our calls here involve Norway rats in basements and alleys, raccoons in chimneys, gray squirrels in triple-decker attics, and big brown bats behind shutters and in old rooflines. Shared walls and adjoining rooflines mean one gap can affect several homes, especially in Cambridgeport and East Cambridge.

In fall and winter, rats and mice push indoors around Central Square and Harvard Square as temperatures drop, while spring brings raccoon mothers looking for quiet chimneys and squirrel litters in attics. Our crew inspects the whole roofline, seals entry points with durable materials, and handles animals from inside the structure on site under Massachusetts PAC rules. Coyotes are seen along the river and Fresh Pond, mostly as background wildlife homeowners ask us about.

faqs.q: How much does wildlife removal cost in Cambridge, MA?
faqs.a: Cost depends on the species, how many entry points the building has, and whether cleanup is needed after animals have been inside, so we inspect first and explain the work before starting. Rat and squirrel jobs in shared multifamily buildings can take more sealing than a single-family home, and we will walk you through what is needed without obligation.

faqs.q: Why do rats keep coming back in Cambridge triple-deckers?
faqs.a: Older triple-deckers often share foundation gaps, utility chases, and adjoining rooflines, and the Charles River corridor and dense alleys give Norway rats food and travel routes. Lasting results come from sealing the building itself, not just removing the rats inside, which is why our crew checks basements, bulkheads, and rear additions on every visit.

Norway rats are a steady problem around older commercial blocks, alleys, and riverfront buildings in The Acre and Centralville.

Spring brings raccoon litters in chimneys and squirrel damage as breeding seasons overlap, and late fall pushes rats, mice, and squirrels indoors before Lowell winters set in. Many Pawtucketville and South Lowell homes back onto wooded or river edges, so skunks under porches and opossums under sheds are common add-ons. We seal the structure, remove animals from inside on site as state rules require, and explain each step before we start.

faqs.q: What does wildlife removal cost in Lowell, MA?

faqs.q: Are bats common in Lowell's older mill-era houses?
faqs.a: Yes. Big brown bats use gaps around old chimneys, eaves, and attic vents in Lowell's 19th- and early-20th-century housing. Bats are handled by exclusion only, and eviction work is limited to May 1 through May 31 or August 1 through October 15 under PAC permit conditions, so timing matters and we plan jobs around those windows.

faqs.q: How much does wildlife removal cost in Newton, MA?

faqs.q: Why are squirrels such a problem in Newton attics?

Once inside they can damage wiring and insulation, so our crew removes them and seals the roofline with materials squirrels cannot chew through.
